title: TCS vs Infosys vs Wipro shares: Despite global AI bloodbath, why are Indian IT stocks rising? Experts decode | Stock Market News
text:
TCS vs Infosys vs Wipro shares: Amid heavy selling in AI stocks in global markets and the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index recording its worst week since 2020 last week, Indian IT stocks have continued to rise. Indian IT majors, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Infosys, Wipro, HCL Technologies, Tech Mahindra, etc., have seen strong buying in the last fortnight. TCS share price today is up by over 3%; Infosys shares also went up around 3% but failed to sustain at higher levels; Wipro shares are trading green after rising up to 2% against Friday's close According to stock market experts, Indian IT stocks are rising despite the global AI bloodbath because capital is rotating out of capital-intensive AI builders and into traditional software and services firms. They said that Indian IT firms do not own expensive chips or data centres. Investors view them as insulated from AI capex blowups. On the reasons that are fueling the Indian IT shares, Avinash Gorakshkar, Founder of Avinash Mentor Research, said, “After steep corrections earlier in 2026—triggered by fears that AI agents would automate outsourcing—large-cap Indian IT stocks fell into oversold territory. Trading at roughly 14x–17x trailing P/E with strong free cash flows, buybacks, and around 2.7%–4.6% dividend yields, they have become defensive value plays.” On reasons for Indian IT majors remaining insulated from the global AI bloodbath, Anuj Gupta, a SEBI-registered market expert, said, “Unlike hyperscalers, Indian IT firms do not own expensive chips or data centers. Investors view them as insulated from AI capex blowups: if AI adoption slows, enterprises still need traditional engineers; if AI scales rapidly, enterprises still need IT integrators to deploy it into legacy systems.” The SEBI-registered market expert said that investors are selling off U.S. chipmakers, cloud giants, and AI labs that have spent hundreds of billions on data centers without clear returns on investment. Capital is rotating out of capital-intensive AI builders and into traditional software and services firms. The Nasdaq 100 fell 10.43% for the week ending November 20, 2026—its worst weekly drop since March 2020—closing at 25,028.98 after a 5.61% plunge on Friday alone. Amid a bloodbath in AI stocks, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite turned negating erasing all its gains in 2026. Shares of NVIDIA, Anthropic, AMD, Broadcom, Micron were among the major drags for the AI bloodbath globally. Comparing the three Indian IT majors, Avinash Gorakshkar said, “TCS commands the largest scale and highest return on equity (~45.9%) among the three Indian IT majors, which is visible in today's rally in the Indian IT shares in the large-cap segment.” However, Mahesh Ojha, VP — Research and Business Development at KC Securities, said, “One should not forget to compare the valuations and price-to-book value of the stock, while adding any stock in portfolio. On this parameter, Wirpo sahres are looking more attractive among the three IT stocks, followed by Infosys, while TCS trades at the highest premium due to its superior return on equity.” However, Ojha also maintained that all three Indian IT stocks are trading well below their historical 5-year valuation averages following the 2026 sector correction. Decoding the technical chart pattern of Wipro shares, Mahesh M Ojha said, “Wipro shares have strong support at ₹168, which is expected to remain sacrosanct. On the upper side, the IT stock is facing resistance at ₹192. On breaking above this resistance on a closing basis, we can expect Wipro share price to come close to ₹205 per share levels.” Speaking on the technical outlook of Infosys shares, Mahesh M Ojha said, "Infosys shares have strong support at ₹1060 followed by ₹1028, which is expected to remain sacrosanct. On the upper side, the IT stock is facing resistance at ₹1145. On breaking above this resistance on a closing basis, we can expect Infosys share price to come close to ₹1200 per share levels.” On the technical outlook for the TCS shares, the KC Securities expert said, "TCS shares have strong support at ₹2350 followed by ₹2280, which is expected to remain sacrosanct. On the upper side, the IT stock is facing resistance at ₹2485. On breaking above this resistance on a closing basis, we can expect Infosys share price to come close to ₹2560 per share levels.” Disclaimer: This story is for educational and informational purposes only.
